title: Component Standard
description: The shared specification-to-stability procedure applied to every FrogUI component.
intro: A component in FrogUI is not complete when its visual layout is drawn. It is complete only when it satisfies all 12 canonical delivery gates across implementation, accessibility, testing, metadata, Showcase, and documentation.

sections.title: Component delivery pipeline
paragraphs: Every component in FrogUI progresses through a rigorous 12-stage delivery pipeline from initial specification to production stability.
Contributors audit existing work, resume at the first incomplete gate, and record evidence in a dedicated delivery record before promoting status:

sections.title: Behavior specification requirement
paragraphs: Implementation never begins with drawing UI. It begins with a comprehensive written specification covering:
• Purpose & scope: What user problem does the component solve? What is explicitly out of scope?
• State ownership: What state is caller-owned? Is a state helper object justified?
• Variants & sizes: What semantic variants exist? What visual sizes are supported?
• Visual states: Default, pressed, focused, disabled, and loading treatments.
• Accessibility: Role announcement, minimum 48dp touch targets, focus rings, TalkBack labels.
• Adaptive behavior: How does the component respond to Compact (< 600dp), Medium (600–839dp), and Expanded (≥ 840dp) window sizes?

sections.title: The 12 canonical delivery gates
paragraphs: Every component is tracked against 12 delivery gates recorded in docs/components/<id>-delivery.md:
1. Specification: Purpose, caller state, variants, sizes, states, interaction, accessibility, and adaptive behavior documented.
2. Public API: Kotlin composable signature, parameter ordering, slot contracts, and theme-aware Defaults designed and reviewed.
3. Implementation: One canonical Compose component built; zero Material, Hugeicons, or demo leaks.
4. Theme / states: Defaults resolve FrogTheme tokens for all variants and visual states.
5. Accessibility: Semantics role, enforced 48dp minimum touch target, visible focus ring, TalkBack annotations.
6. Compose previews: FrogComponentPreview renders variants, sizes, states, dark theme, and customization.
7. Automated tests: JVM unit tests and Compose semantics/activation/restoration tests pass.
8. Registry metadata: JSON record created with schema v2 lifecycle evidence, properties, and routes.
9. Showcase integration: ComponentShowcaseDefinition supplies component, typed controls, and inspector to ComponentDetailScreen.
10. Web documentation: Shared ComponentDetailPage renders prose, API property tables, and registered preview.
11. API compatibility: Binary ABI baseline established in api/<module>.api; passes apiCheck.
12. Visual regression: High-value native screen captures and deterministic pixel assertions verified.

sections.title: FrogButton reference implementation
paragraphs: FrogButton serves as the canonical reference for simple action controls in FrogUI.

It provides 5 semantic variants (Primary, Secondary, Outline, Ghost, Destructive), 3 sizes (Small 32dp, Medium 40dp, Large 48dp), and 5 visual states (default, pressed, focused, disabled, loading). While visual height can be 32dp or 40dp, the clickable touch target is enforced at >= 48dp by the runtime contract.

sections.title: FrogDrawer reference implementation
paragraphs: FrogDrawer serves as the canonical reference for complex overlay controls in FrogUI.

It demonstrates adaptive presentation (automatically switching between Bottom Sheet on Compact displays and Side Drawer on Medium/Expanded displays), focus trapping, scrim dismissal, Back handler integration, and saveable state management via FrogDrawerState.

sections.title: Shared Showcase architecture
paragraphs: FrogUI rejects bespoke screen designs for different components in the Showcase.

All components are presented through a single, unified ComponentDetailScreen shell in the :app module. Each component provides a ComponentShowcaseDefinition supplying live preview composables, typed property controls, inspector drawers, and code generators.

sections.title: Shared web docs architecture
paragraphs: Similarly, the web documentation platform renders all component pages through a single, shared ComponentDetailPage component.
The page dynamically renders the component prose, interactive preview canvas, generated API property tables, accessibility guidance, and delivery status badges from catalog.json.

sections.title: Stability promotion gates
paragraphs: Component maturity is governed by strict, validator-enforced lifecycle statuses:
• Experimental: Working implementation with verified core behaviors; may retain partial or deferred gates.
• Beta: Feature-complete implementation; cannot contain missing, outdated, or duplicated delivery gates.
• Stable: Every single gate of the 12 canonical delivery gates must be COMPLETE, accompanied by an approved docs/components/<id>-review.md stability record and binary compatibility baselines.

callout.title: Automated Promotion Enforcement
callout.value: The registry validator (tools/registry/registry.mjs) inspects docs/components/<id>-delivery.md on every build. It actively rejects any component claiming Stable status if any gate remains incomplete.

sections.title: Component Definition of Done
paragraphs: Before any component is merged or promoted in FrogUI, maintainers verify this complete Definition of Done checklist:
bullets: Specification: Purpose, state ownership, and variants documented in a delivery record.
API: Follows canonical parameter ordering; slot names are vendor-neutral; Defaults resolve FrogTheme.
Implementation: Pure Compose; zero Material leaks; zero Hugeicons or network dependencies.
Accessibility: ≥ 48dp touch envelope guaranteed; visible 2dp focus ring; TalkBack tested.
Testing: JVM unit tests for state machines; Compose tests for semantics and activation.
Registry: Validated against schema v2; source paths, examples, and routes verified.
Showcase: Integrated into ComponentDetailScreen with typed controls and live preview.
Docs: Component prose authored; API table generated; preview registered.
Compatibility: Release AAR ABI extracted and verified against baseline with apiCheck.

title: Registry
description: A machine-readable metadata layer that keeps component identity, discovery, documentation, and tooling synchronized.
intro: The FrogUI registry is a build-time metadata contract that synchronizes component discovery across the native Android showcase, web documentation, search indices, and validation tooling. It does not render UI or execute at runtime.

sections.title: Why a registry exists
paragraphs: In multi-surface design systems, maintaining component lists, API properties, interactive routes, and documentation separately leads inevitably to documentation drift.

The FrogUI registry solves this by establishing a single machine-readable source of truth for component metadata in registry/components/<id>.json. From this structured metadata, build tooling automatically projects typed discovery models for both Android and the Web:

sections.title: The registry does not implement UI
paragraphs: It is critical to understand what the registry is NOT: the registry is NOT a server-driven UI engine, layout definition, or runtime widget factory.

The registry stores descriptive facts about components—their names, categories, status, parameters, accessible roles, and example snippet bounds. It contains zero Compose rendering logic, zero UI layout trees, and zero JSON-to-Composable reflection.

callout.title: Registry Scope Boundary
callout.value: Registry JSON ≠ UI definition. FrogUI never interprets JSON into Compose UI at runtime. All user interface execution happens strictly through compiled Kotlin composables.

sections.title: Component ID contract
paragraphs: Every component possesses a stable, lowercase, kebab-case identifier (such as button or drawer).

This ID forms an immutable contract across the entire ecosystem: registry JSON filename (registry/components/button.json), Android Showcase destination route (/components/button), web documentation URL (/components/button), delivery record (docs/components/button-delivery.md), and future CLI commands (frogui add button).

sections.title: Registry entry anatomy
paragraphs: Component records adhere to Schema Version 2 (component.schema.json). Here is the actual structured anatomy of a canonical record:

code.title: registry/components/button.json structure
code.value:
{
  "$schema": "../schema/component.schema.json",
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "id": "button",
  "name": "FrogButton",
  "displayName": "Button",
  "description": "Trigger an action or event with explicit visual hierarchy and accessible states.",
  "category": "actions",
  "status": "experimental",
  "since": "0.1.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "source": "frogui-components/src/main/java/io/github/codewitheswar/frogui/components/actions/button/FrogButton.kt",
  "showcase": {
    "route": "/components/button",
    "source": "app/src/main/java/io/github/codewitheswar/frogui/showcase/components/button/ButtonShowcaseDefinition.kt",
    "screen": "io.github.codewitheswar.frogui.showcase.components.button.ButtonShowcaseDefinition"
  },
  "variants": ["Primary", "Secondary", "Outline", "Ghost", "Destructive"],
  "sizes": ["Small", "Medium", "Large"],
  "properties": [
    { "name": "onClick", "type": "() -> Unit", "defaultValue": "required", "description": "Callback triggered on click." },
    { "name": "variant", "type": "FrogButtonVariant", "defaultValue": "FrogButtonVariant.Primary", "description": "Visual hierarchy variant." }
  ],
  "accessibility": {
    "role": "Role.Button",
    "minTouchTarget": "48.dp",
    "talkBackNotes": "Announces button role, enabled/disabled state, and loading progress."
  }
}

sections.title: Draft-07 JSON schemas
paragraphs: The registry uses three formal Draft-07 schemas in registry/schema/:
• component.schema.json: Validates component records, requiring identity, paths, status, variants, properties, and schema v2 lifecycle evidence.
• example.schema.json: Validates compilable code example descriptors.
• registry.schema.json: Validates the top-level index (registry/index.json) containing category taxonomy and component ordering.

sections.title: Generated outputs & projections
paragraphs: Build tools process registry JSON and produce typed models for consumption:
1. frogui-registry/build/.../GeneratedComponentRegistry.kt: Kotlin data structures consumed by the Showcase for offline search, category listing, and navigation dispatch.
2. docs/dist/catalog.json & search.json: Static JSON datasets containing full component metadata and search indexes for the web docs.
3. docs/src/generated/catalog.ts & searchIndex.ts: Typed TypeScript interfaces and arrays for Vite frontend development.

sections.title: Showcase integration
paragraphs: The native Android Showcase does not maintain hardcoded lists of components or screens. Instead, it queries FrogComponentRegistry at runtime to discover available components, display category counts, and route users to the appropriate ComponentDetailScreen.

sections.title: Web docs integration
paragraphs: The web documentation site uses the generated catalog data to populate sidebar navigation, render API property tables, display status badges, and power the instant search dialog (Cmd/Ctrl + K).

sections.title: Automated registry validation
paragraphs: Running npm run registry:validate executes tools/registry/registry.mjs with comprehensive checks:
• Validates JSON against Draft-07 schemas via Ajv.
• Verifies source file paths exist within the repository.
• Performs lexical checks verifying Kotlin parameter names, types, defaults, and ordering match source code.
• Verifies referenced example regions exist in compiled Showcase source files.
• Enforces delivery record existence and promotion criteria for Beta and Stable components.

sections.title: Registry vs Kotlin vs Markdown
paragraphs: FrogUI maintains a clean separation of concerns across its three content representations:
• Kotlin Source: The authoritative runtime implementation and public API contract.
• Registry JSON: Machine-readable facts (identity, properties, status, evidence paths, routes).
• Markdown Docs: Long-form human guidance, design rationale, architectural principles, and layout examples.

sections.title: Future CLI integration (Planned)
paragraphs: A future command-line interface (frogui CLI) is planned to leverage the registry for developer workflows:
• frogui init: Configures dependencies and theme wrappers in consumer Android projects.
• frogui add <component-id>: Copies or configures component source modules.
These capabilities are planned and not currently usable in the current 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT release.

title: Release Architecture
description: How FrogUI validates source, APIs, registry metadata, documentation, and published artifacts before a release.
intro: FrogUI enforces strict release verification where no artifact is published until compilation, binary ABI checks, registry schemas, tests, and documentation builds pass with zero errors.

sections.title: Release philosophy & safety
paragraphs: Releasing a design system library requires significantly higher verification standards than typical application releases. Once a library version is consumed by external apps, bugs, broken ABI contracts, or missing tokens cannot be easily patched without forcing breaking changes on downstream teams.
FrogUI release philosophy is built on three unbreakable rules:
1. Atomic gate enforcement: If any verification gate fails, release execution stops immediately.
2. Truthful metadata: Version numbers and publication statuses must never claim remote release before it occurs.
3. Zero manual drift: Published AARs, documentation, registry metadata, and API baselines must come from the exact same verified git commit.

sections.title: End-to-end release pipeline
paragraphs: A change moves from pull request to verified staging through a structured pipeline:

sections.title: Pull request verification gates
paragraphs: Every pull request targeting main triggers automated verification across Android and web stacks:
• Android CI: Compiles release classes, executes JVM unit tests, runs Android Lint, and verifies API baselines.
• Docs CI: Validates registry schemas, typechecks TypeScript, builds the static Vite bundle, and verifies 404/base-path integrity.
Pull requests cannot be merged while any CI check is red.

sections.title: Android CI pipeline
paragraphs: The .github/workflows/android-ci.yml workflow runs on Ubuntu with Temurin JDK 21 and Android SDK 36.1:
It executes: bash gradlew verifyArchitecture apiCheck testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest :frogui-theme:assembleDebugAndroidTest
This validates dependency boundaries, public API compatibility, state machine logic, static lint checks, and test APK compilation in a single unified run.

sections.title: Documentation CI pipeline
paragraphs: The .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml workflow runs on Node 24:
It executes: npm run registry:validate, npm test, npm run docs:typecheck, and npm run docs:build.
Post-build verification scripts verify that docs/dist/index.html, 404.html, catalog.json, and search.json exist and correctly reference the /FrogUI/ base path.

sections.title: Public API compatibility gate
paragraphs: The apiCheck task ensures that no accidental or unreviewed changes leak into public library interfaces.

During build, release AAR bytecodes are analyzed, normalized, and compared against api/<module>.api baselines. If a public class, method, or parameter changes, the build fails with an explicit diff. Only an explicit maintainer action (./gradlew apiDump) can update baselines.

sections.title: Registry validation gate
paragraphs: The validateRegistry Gradle task (node tools/registry/generate.mjs --validate) runs as a mandatory dependency of verifyArchitecture.
It catches schema violations, missing source files, invalid routes, or out-of-sync parameter signatures before any build artifact is assembled.

sections.title: Versioning strategy & release.properties
paragraphs: Version information is centralized in gradle/release.properties:
• version: The library SemVer coordinate (currently 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT).
• versionCode: Integer version code for the Android Showcase application (currently 1).
• published: Boolean flag tracking whether this version has been uploaded to a remote repository (currently false).
Build tools, Gradle coordinates, Showcase version banners, and generated documentation read this single file.

sections.title: Local artifact staging (publishAllPublicationsToBuildRepository)
paragraphs: FrogUI includes full Maven publication configuration in FrogPublishingPlugin, wired to an ignored local repository in build/maven:

Running ./gradlew publishAllPublicationsToBuildRepository packages release AARs, sources JARs, POM files (with license, developer, and SCM metadata), and Gradle module metadata for :frogui-foundation, :frogui-theme, and :frogui-components.
This enables maintainers to inspect packaged artifacts, POM dependencies, and classes before any remote release action.

code.title: Staging Maven Publications Locally
code.value:
# Package and stage release artifacts locally:
./gradlew publishAllPublicationsToBuildRepository

# Inspect staged output:
ls build/maven/io/github/codewitheswar/

sections.title: GitHub Releases
paragraphs: Official releases correspond to signed git tags (e.g. v0.1.0). Each release includes release notes detailing new components, API updates, accessibility notes, and breaking changes or migration guides.

sections.title: Maven Central distribution (Planned)
paragraphs: Remote distribution to Maven Central is planned for the 0.1.0 stable release.
Remote publishing will require GPG signing keys, Sonatype Central credentials, and automated validation via GitHub Secrets. Secret keys and credentials are never stored in repository files.

sections.title: GitHub Pages deployment
paragraphs: Documentation deployment is decoupled from library publication. The docs-deploy.yml workflow deploys the documentation site to GitHub Pages on every push to main.
This ensures that documentation updates, guides, and fixes are published immediately without requiring a new library version bump.

sections.title: Failure handling & recovery
paragraphs: If any CI check or release gate fails during release staging:
1. Publication is halted immediately; no partial artifacts are uploaded.
2. The root cause (compile failure, ABI mismatch, registry error, broken link) is identified and resolved in a new commit.
3. The full verification suite is re-executed from a clean state.
Partially publishing mismatched library versions or out-of-sync documentation is strictly forbidden.

sections.title: Production release checklist
paragraphs: Maintainers follow this checklist prior to cutting a release:
bullets: 1. Component Status: All promoted components satisfy delivery gates in docs/components/<id>-delivery.md.
2. Architecture Verification: ./gradlew verifyArchitecture passes with 0 errors.
3. API Compatibility: ./gradlew apiCheck passes against version-controlled .api baselines.
4. Registry Validation: npm run registry:validate confirms 0 schema or route errors.
5. Tests: JVM unit tests, Compose tests, and Node test suites pass.
6. Documentation: npm run docs:build succeeds and static output integrity is verified.
7. Local Staging: ./gradlew publishAllPublicationsToBuildRepository succeeds; POMs inspected in build/maven.
8. Version Bump: gradle/release.properties updated with target version and tag created.
